Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Audit logging language for RFP library — align with current product + disclaimers

Team — we keep getting inconsistent answers on audit logging in RFPs (Nordbank + Aurora both asked for “SIEM export, admin actions, retention, immutability”).

Can we align today on:
1) What we can *truthfully* claim for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
2) What we should explicitly *not* claim (roadmap)
3) The standard snippet to drop into the RFP library + FAQ

I’ve attached the current draft snippet that SEs are using (v3) and the event taxonomy table Markus pulled together.

Specific questions I need confirmed:
- Are audit logs covering console + API admin actions (API keys, users/roles, org settings, model deployments, routing policy changes)?
- Export destinations: do we support S3 export today for Dedicated/Private? What about Hosted?
- Retention: do customers choose retention and is it per-deployment? How should we word “configurable”?
- Do audit logs include prompt/response content? (I believe no; request logs are separate / gated)

Goal: approved language by EOD so Isabelle can push to the snippet tool + Confluence index.

— Naomi
Product Security PM
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RFP-snippet_Audit-Logging_v3.docx
Attachment: audit-log-event-taxonomy_2026-01-29.csv

Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 9:33 AM PST
Subject: Re: Audit logging language for RFP library — align with current product + disclaimers

+1 to tightening this.

Field context: the question is *always* “audit logs” but they often mean 3 different things:
A) Admin audit trail (who changed what in Console / Admin API)
B) Request logging (per inference request metadata) + trace IDs
C) Content logging (prompts/responses)

SEs have been answering with a blended A+B and it gets us in trouble.

My take based on current behavior:
- Audit log (A): yes for Console actions; also includes Admin API actions (API keys created/rotated, user invited/removed, role changes, project creation, routing policy edits, model deployment edits). Not exhaustive for every endpoint yet.
- Export: Dedicated/Private can push to customer S3 bucket (we’ve implemented for a few customers). Hosted export is “download via API” today, not continuous shipping.
- Retention: Hosted is fixed by plan; Dedicated/Private can set longer retention (esp. compliance pack). I would avoid “fully configurable” unless we can specify bounds.

Marcus/Kevin — can you confirm the export + retention wording and what’s safe to claim?

— Markus
Solutions Engineering Lead

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 10:07 AM PST
Subject: Re: Audit logging language for RFP library — align with current product + disclaimers

Confirming what we can safely say *today*:

Scope / events
- We have an “Audit Log” feature for administrative events in the Redwood Console and Admin API.
- Includes: authentication events (console login), user lifecycle (invite/deactivate), role changes, API key lifecycle, project/workspace settings changes, model deployment changes, routing policy changes, and certain billing/org settings updates.
- It does NOT currently log every possible read-only action (e.g., viewing a page) and we shouldn’t imply “all actions” or “full session recording.”

Export
- Dedicated + Private: supported export to customer-controlled destinations is available. For now, the supported/validated path is periodic export to customer-managed S3-compatible object storage (customer-owned bucket, customer-controlled IAM). We also have a couple of SIEM integrations via customer-side collectors consuming the exported objects.
- Hosted: customers can access audit logs in the Console; API access exists for retrieval. We do not have guaranteed real-time push / webhook shipping for Hosted as a standard capability. Don’t promise “streaming to SIEM” for Hosted.

Retention
- Retention is plan/deployment dependent. We can offer extended retention as part of enterprise/compliance packaging; default retention is not “indefinite.”
- Wording suggestion: “retention periods are configurable within defined ranges based on deployment mode and plan; longer retention available for enterprise/compliance needs.”

Content
- Audit logs are *administrative metadata* and should not contain customer prompt/response content.

Roadmap disclaimer
- If asked about “immutable/WORM,” we can say we protect integrity of logs and restrict modification via RBAC, but do NOT claim WORM/SEC17a-4 compliant unless Legal/GRC explicitly signs off.

Kevin can add detail on exact fields.

— Marcus
Security Engineering

From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 10:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Audit logging language for RFP library — align with current product + disclaimers

Adding specifics (what the logs actually look like).

Audit log entry fields (typical)
- Timestamp (UTC)
- Actor (user id / service principal), actor email if available
- Actor IP (where available)
- Action (event name)
- Target object type + id (e.g., api_key, user, deployment, routing_policy)
- Result (success/failure) and error code
- Request id / trace id for correlation

Important nuance:
- For some events we store “before/after” *metadata diffs* (e.g., routing policy updated) but not sensitive values (e.g., API key material).
- For exports to customer storage, we export JSON lines files with a stable schema and version it. We should avoid promising “real-time” or “exactly-once” semantics.

On “immutability”:
- In-product, audit log entries are append-only from the application perspective. Admin users cannot edit audit log events in the Console.
- That said, we should not call it “tamper-proof” or “immutable ledger.” If customers ask, we can discuss controls (access controls, monitoring, backups) and for Dedicated/Private they can store exported logs in their own WORM-capable storage if they need.

Proposed safe sentence:
“Customers can export audit log events to customer-controlled object storage for independent retention and immutability controls.”

— Kevin
Security Controls SME

Subject: Re: Audit logging language for RFP library — align with current product + disclaimers

Private deployment nuance (since Nordbank is pushing on this):

- In Private (VPC/on-prem), the control plane still emits audit log events; the customer can choose export target inside their network boundary.
- We should be careful with “customer-managed keys” phrasing: that’s encryption/KMS; audit logging export is separate. For Private, customers can enforce their own encryption-at-rest and retention on the destination side.
- For “data residency”: audit logs are part of the same residency boundary as the control plane region / private deployment footprint. Don’t imply global replication.

If we need a one-liner for RFP:
“Private deployments support audit log export to customer-controlled storage within the customer’s network boundary.”

— Colin
Private Deployment SME

Subject: Re: Audit logging language for RFP library — align with current product + disclaimers

Thanks all — here’s the consolidated language I’m going to mark as “approved” for the RFP library (unless objections by noon).

RFP snippet (approved draft)
“Redwood provides Audit Logs for administrative actions performed in the Redwood Console and Admin API (e.g., user and role management, API key lifecycle, project/org settings changes, model deployment changes, and routing policy updates). Audit log entries include metadata such as timestamp, actor identity, action, target object, and result. Audit logs are designed to record administrative activity and do not include customer prompt/response content.

Access to audit logs is governed by role-based access controls. Export options depend on deployment mode: Dedicated and Private deployments support export of audit log events to customer-controlled S3-compatible object storage (and can be forwarded to a customer SIEM via customer-managed integrations). Hosted deployments support viewing audit logs in the Console and retrieval via API; real-time push/streaming export is not a standard Hosted capability.

Retention periods are deployment-mode and plan dependent, with extended retention available for enterprise/compliance needs. Customers may also retain exported logs in their own storage according to their internal retention and immutability requirements.”

Explicit “don’t say” notes (to add as comments for Sales/SE)
- Don’t claim “all actions are logged” (use “administrative actions” + examples)
- Don’t claim “real-time SIEM integration” for Hosted
- Don’t claim WORM/SEC17a-4 compliance or “tamper-proof ledger”
- Don’t imply prompt/response content is in audit logs

Action items
- Elliot: please ensure PR-2849 aligns with the above phrasing (esp. Hosted export caveat)
- Markus: once I post this to the RFP library, please tell the team to stop using v3 doc attachment
- I’ll update the standard answers page + ping Isabelle for snippet tool rollout (PM-4829)

— Naomi
Product Security PM
Redwood Inference
